confidence_notes: Restaurant, coffee and beer anchors are based on several aggregated web sources. These include Numbeo-based averages from about mid-2026: an inexpensive meal at about EUR 12.5, a mid-range three-course meal for two at about EUR 47, a cappuccino at about EUR 2.2 and a draught beer at about EUR 2–3.1. Weekday set lunch menus (menú del día) are reported at about EUR 12–15. The beer anchor is a blend, because a typical local caña is smaller and cheaper than the 0.5 L Numbeo serving. Cocktail and wine evidence is thinner, mostly travel guides of mixed quality. They suggest about EUR 6–9 for a simple cocktail and about EUR 2–4 for a glass of house or local wine, so I took midpoints and cross-checked them against the beer price. Prices are converted at roughly 1.10 USD per EUR, an approximate rate that adds some uncertainty for the July 2026 window. All four accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge only; I did not search or check any listings. July is a relatively low season in Córdoba because of extreme summer heat, so room rates are assumed to be below the spring peak (the May patio festival). Accommodation is the least certain part of this estimate. Venues next to the Mezquita charge noticeably more than these typical anchors.
comparable_city_reasoning: Córdoba is one of the cheaper Andalusian tourist cities for eating out, roughly in line with Granada and somewhat cheaper than Seville or Málaga. The accommodation estimates are based on mid-sized Andalusian heritage cities in the summer shoulder or low season.
